header: xTeleport: every teleport your server needs.
Apply changes with /xteleport reload (or /xtp reload). Everything applies except
storage, even turning commands on or off. A bad value falls back to its default with
a warning in the console; xTeleport never stops over config. The messages are in lang/.

comment: How this plugin's messages look, and the language they're in. shared uses the
setting in plugins/Xena/config.yml, which every Xena plugin reads; anything else is
this plugin's own.
The language players see messages in: auto for each player's own (their client's
language setting), or one language for everyone, such as de or pt-BR.
The language of the console, and of players whose language has no file in lang/.
The look every message shares, used in messages as tags: <prefix>, <highlight>,
<success> and <error>. Colours are names (gray, gold) or hex (#B48CFF), with bold,
italic, underlined, strikethrough or obfuscated if you like: <#B48CFF><bold>.
<prefix> starts the default messages. Make it your server's name, such as
"<dark_gray>[<gradient:#B48CFF:#5EE08A>MyServer</gradient>]</dark_gray> ", or blank for none.
The colour of message text that has no tag of its own.
<highlight>: names and values, such as a player or a speed.
<success>: something turned on or done.
<error>: something refused or turned off.
Every command has the same settings:
enabled            false removes the command entirely, so another plugin can have its name
aliases            other names for it
permission         needed to use it; blank ("") lets anyone
permission-others  needed to use it on another player's homes
Commands that teleport also have:
cooldown           seconds before it can be used again; xteleport.cooldown.bypass skips it
cost               what each teleport costs, through xMoney (or Vault's economy);
xteleport.cost.bypass skips it. Taken once the warmup is over, and
given back if the teleport fails.
/sethome [name]: sets a home where you stand. Setting one again moves it.
/home [name]: with one home, or one called home, the name can be left out.
/delhome <name>
/homes [page]: a list to click. Staff with permission-others: /homes <player>.
/tpa <player>: ask to teleport to someone. The cost is paid by whoever asked.
/tpahere <player>: ask someone to teleport to you.
/tpaccept [player]: the newest request, or the one from that player.
/tpacancel [player]: takes back requests you sent.
/tptoggle: stop or start getting requests.
/warp [name]: without a name, lists the warps.
/rtp [world]
How every teleport behaves.
Seconds to stand still before teleporting. 0 teleports at once. xteleport.warmup.bypass skips it.
Whether taking damage during the warmup cancels it, as moving does.
Refuse to send players somewhere that is now in lava, inside blocks, over the void,
high in the air or outside the world border, with a message instead of a death:
homes, warps, the spawn, and the player a TPA goes to. The spot's chunk is loaded
in the background to check, never on the server's thread where the server can.
With check-safe, the most blocks a player may fall on arriving. Falls of 3 or less
don't hurt. Water below is safe from any height.
How many homes a player may have. A player with xteleport.homes.<n> may have <n>
instead, and xteleport.homes.unlimited any number; the highest wins.
More limits, by permission. A blank permission means group.<name>, which LuckPerms
gives every member of that group, so vip: below works for a LuckPerms group called vip.
The home /sethome sets, and /home goes to, when no name is given.
Let players go to their bed or respawn anchor with /home <bed-name>. It doesn't count
towards their limit, and shows first in /homes.
Homes per page in /homes.
Seconds before a request runs out.
Each warp needs xteleport.warp.<name> (operators have them all). /warps only lists
the ones a player may use.
Warps per page in /warps.
Send players who join for the first time to the spawn set with /setspawn.
Send every player there each time they join.
Send players there when they die without a bed or respawn anchor.
/rtp: a random safe spot.
Where /rtp sends players who don't name a world. Blank means the world they're in, if
/rtp may send them there.
Spots tried before giving up. Each loads one chunk in the background.
Seconds before a player can start another search, whether it found a spot or not,
so nobody can keep the server busy generating chunks. The cooldown under
commands.rtp is the longer wait, after arriving. xteleport.cooldown.bypass skips both.
How many /rtp searches may run at once, server-wide. Anyone over it is told to try
again in a few seconds, so a crowd typing /rtp can't slow the server.
Only pick chunks that already exist, so /rtp never makes the server generate terrain.
Best for worlds pre-generated with a plugin such as Chunky.
Biomes /rtp never picks, as Minecraft names them.
The worlds /rtp may send players to, by name, and where. A world that isn't listed
can't be picked. The Nether is searched below its roof, and the End off its main
island unless allow-main-island is true. Each world has:
enabled            false keeps /rtp out of this world
permission         needed to /rtp into this world; blank lets anyone
center-on-spawn    measure from the world's spawn point, or from center-x and center-z
min-radius         the nearest and farthest a spot may be from the centre, in blocks;
max-radius         the world border also limits it
allow-main-island  the End only: allow spots on the main island, where the dragon is
On Fabric, a world's name is its dimension: minecraft:overworld, minecraft:the_nether,
minecraft:the_end; world, world_nether and world_the_end mean those there too.
entries.defaultText: {world: {enabled: true, permission: "", center-on-spawn: true, center-x: 0, center-z: 0, min-radius: 300, max-radius: 5000, allow-main-island: false}, world_nether: {enabled: true, permission: "", center-on-spawn: true, center-x: 0, center-z: 0, min-radius: 100, max-radius: 1000, allow-main-island: false}, world_the_end: {enabled: true, permission: "", center-on-spawn: false, center-x: 0, center-z: 0, min-radius: 1100, max-radius: 4000, allow-main-island: false}}

comment: Where this plugin keeps its data. Read at startup only: restart after changing it.
sqlite keeps everything in one file in the plugin's folder, with nothing to set up.
mysql (or MariaDB) is for networks, or servers with a lot of history.
shared keeps it in the database every Xena plugin can share, set in plugins/Xena/config.yml.
Put in front of every table's name, so plugins and servers can share one database.
Only for type: mysql.
Extra connection settings, as in a JDBC URL: useSSL=true&serverTimezone=UTC.
The connections used to read, beside the one that writes.
How many: 0 picks for the database (1 for SQLite, 2 for MySQL). More helps only a
MySQL server that many reads wait on.
Telling you when a newer version is out: in the console, and to players with
<plugin>.admin.update when they join. Asks Modrinth once a day, off the server's threads,
sending only the plugin's version, the platform and the Minecraft version.
Whether to ask at all.
Which releases to hear of: release, beta (betas and releases) or alpha (everything).
